atoms.text: Felipe says: “My high school in the USA had school rules just like my school in Germany. There are some rules that were the same at my American and my German high school. However, there are also some rules that we had at my American high school and that did not exist in my high school in Germany.”

atoms.text: Felipe says: “A rule that I did not expect was the dress code. In school, we were not allowed to wear whatever we wanted. For instance, our clothes should not be too short or too tight. My friend Kyle wasn't even allowed to wear his sweatpants. Once he arrived at school wearing them and a teacher saw and sent him back home to change his clothes.”

atoms.text: Felipe says: “There was a rule that surprised me even more than the dress code. We were only allowed to be in the hallways during breaks. During the lessons we were supposed to be in the classrooms. If we needed to leave the classroom and walk through the hallways during class time, we were expected to ask the teacher and get a hall pass from them. So, if we wanted to go to the lockers or to the toilet, we needed to have a hall pass.”

atoms.text: Felipe says: “There was another rule that was a bit annoying. We were supposed to have a student ID with us all the time. That rule isn't too complicated, but I'm so forgetful. That meant, I often didn't remember to bring it with me. Whether we were in the school cafeteria, in the classroom or in the hallways, we were expected to have our student ID's by our side.”

atoms.text: Felipe says: “If pupils got caught breaking any of the rules, they got into trouble. They had to see the headmaster and got a punishment. At my school, the pupils often got detention when they went against the school rules. Sometimes, they even were suspended for a couple of days. So, it was definitely not a good idea to break the rules, whether it was intentional or not.”
